  11 │ The version I print should keep the numbers exactly as I wrote them. If I
  12 │ write a trailing zero, it stays. If I write a full release number followed by
  13 │ an alpha tag or a release tag, that full release number stays with it. At the
  14 │ same time, the short form and the long form of the same release should still
  15 │ count as the same version when they are compared.
  16 │ 
  17 │ ## About this project
  18 │ This project is a small library for working with the version numbers of
  19 │ software packages. It reads a version written as text, compares two versions,
  20 │ and prints a version back. People use it to check and sort the versions listed
  21 │ in their project files.
  22 │ 
  23 │ ## Problem this solves
  24 │ When a version is printed in a shortened form, I cannot match it against the
  25 │ version I wrote in my project file, so I cannot be sure the tool read the right
  26 │ thing. Keeping the numbers as written removes that confusion.

  29 │ The release part of a version now keeps every number the user typed instead of
  30 │ dropping the trailing zeros, and the plain part of a version keeps those zeros
  31 │ too. The examples in the docs and the expected values in the tests now keep
  32 │ those zeros as well. Comparing versions still treats the short form and the
  33 │ long form of the same release as equal.
  34 │ 
  35 │ ## Impact
  36 │ Correctness and ease of use of the version text shown to people, with no
  37 │ change to how versions are compared or sorted.

  40 │ Before: I print a version written as one point zero and the tool shows just
